text:
Recent evidence supports testing diagnostic correctness separately from recommendation accuracy. A [2024 metamorphic-testing study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) exposed reliability problems across LibRec, PREA, and Surprise using input transformations with expected output relationships. This supports controlled checks, but does not establish that diagnostic-driven training changes improve BERT4Rec. Proposed task-specific controls: inject incorrect left-padding readout, target leakage, or mask-token misuse into isolated diagnostic fixtures; verify detection and recovery after correction. Include unchanged-model controls to measure false alarms. These are proposed experiments, not published findings for this benchmark.

Sampled ranking and full-catalog behavior require separate interpretation. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) evaluates sampling through fidelity, separability, exposure robustness, and predictive power. Earlier [sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) demonstrates that sampling can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Therefore, training-prefix reconstruction measures fit; pinned 99-negative validation HR@10 measures the host objective; full-catalog unseen-item recommendations describe another ranking setting. Improvements in one do not establish improvements in the others.

For uncertainty, compare baseline and candidate on identical validation users and candidates. Proposed analysis: bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category, then average the four category differences equally; report the macro gain and 95% interval. [Search/recommendation significance research](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale) supports bootstrap/randomization approaches and emphasizes effect size. Such intervals condition on the fixed users/candidates and trained models; they do not capture training-seed variation or remove adaptive-search optimism. Judge diagnostic usefulness by whether prespecified repairs improve unchanged host validation HR@10, using no test labels or additional fitted predictors.
